meta.purpose: Real, sourced data for filling a car at a named station and charging an EV at a named charger in SLATE's eight towns, beside the regional averages in content/vehiclefees.ts (FUEL) and content/evcatalog.ts (CHARGING).

statusValues.verified: read from the primary source for that exact station, charger, model or figure
statusValues.verified-govdata: read from a government open-data feed or locator (AFDC/NREL station API, fueleconomy.gov, NRCan, CNE, Statistics Canada, Ontario)
statusValues.secondhand: read from an aggregator or press (GasBuddy, Zapmap, PlugShare, checkfuelprices, DCFC Tracker, EVKX, Infobae, search summaries)
statusValues.estimate: derived here; the entry says how
statusValues.none: nothing found; the area average applies

meta.snapshotWarning: Every price is a dated snapshot, not a live price.
notes: London: both Esso sites are run by Motor Fuel Group and appear in MFG's statutory feed, not Esso's. The game's "Esso, Marylebone Road" is matched to MFG Dorset House, 170 Marylebone Road, NW1 5AR, the only Esso on that road in any feed checked.

statusKey.verified: operator's own page for that site or network
statusKey.verified-govdata: US DOE AFDC station data (open API, now served at developer.nlr.gov after NREL's rename); AFDC 'TESLA' = NACS/J3400, 'J1772COMBO' = CCS1, 'J1772' = J1772 AC
statusKey.secondhand: aggregator (Zapmap, DCFC Tracker, Irish Times, trade press, search-index snippet of an operator page)

chargerConventions.afdcNote: AFDC queries were made with DEMO_KEY at developer.nlr.gov/api/alt-fuel-stations/v1/nearest.json; the key hit its hourly limit (429) before Electrify Canada / Petro-Canada / Ivy could be queried by network in Canada. AFDC 'max power' is the per-port power_kw in ev_charging_units. AFDC ev_pricing was empty for most sites; where it was filled it is quoted verbatim.

premiumRequired._basis: US and Canada: the official EPA/DOE fueleconomy.gov web service and NRCan's 2026 Fuel Consumption Ratings open data (updated 2026-09-28), which list each engine's fuel (EPA: Regular / Midgrade / Premium Gasoline; NRCan: X regular, Z premium, D diesel, E E85). Neither separates "premium required" from "premium recommended"; only the owner's manual does, and no owner's manual was read for a North American model. Europe: these mass-market engines are rated on 95 RON standard unleaded (E10); none is known to require 98 RON super. The luxury/performance makes named in the brief (BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Porsche, Lexus) are not in CAR_MODELS at all; the only premium-fuel engines in the catalog's model lines are optional ones (GM 6.2 L V8, Ram 3.0 L Hurricane HO/RHO, Ford Raptor R 5.2 L), not the trims SLATE sells.

general.statement: AFDC: DC fast charging gives "approximately 100 to 200+ miles of range per 30 minutes of charging"; "charging power varies by vehicle and battery state of charge". DOE (via search summary): most batteries reduce charging power between 80 and 100 percent during fast charging.
general.status: verified for the two AFDC sentences; secondhand for the 80-100% sentence (not found on an opened DOE page)

stateGuidance.statement: Drive Electric Minnesota FAQ: a 2020 Model 3 Long Range on a 250 kW V3 Supercharger reaches about 23% in 5 minutes, "80 percent in about 20 minutes, and 100 percent in less than 25 minutes"; 350 kW stations charge 100 kWh+ packs "to 80 percent in about 15 minutes"; "vehicles take longer to charge in cold weather".

curves.note: Charge curves from EVKX.net, an aggregator of published charging tests, for the catalog's own cars. Each point is [state of charge %, kW, cumulative time from 0% (m:ss)] on a charger that is not the limit. Usable directly as a kW-by-SoC lookup.

chevrolet-equinox-ev-fwd.note: evkx gives 89 kWh; GM sells an 85 kWh pack. Its printed 10-80% time (36:46) agrees with the table (42:40 - 5:53).

ford-puma-gen-e.note: Ford UK itself says 10-80% in 26 minutes. The table's 0-10% rows are anomalous (1 kW at 0%) and are left out.

modelSuggestion.derivation: Read off the curves above, not published as a rule: at 80% the car draws 26-50% of its peak (Model Y LFP 46/175, Panasonic 60/225, Equinox 65/150, Puma 50/100), and 80 to 100% takes 24-43 minutes, about as long as or longer than 10 to 80%. A per-car piecewise-linear kW-by-SoC lookup, capped by the charger's kW, reproduces those times; one rule for all cars would not.
